C1.target: Delayed emergence and persistence of segmented internal cavity area in transcribing RNA droplets, with unresolved B/A cause.
known_relations: E0: at 24 h A=.004458 and B=.089183 mean segmented area fraction; seven fields per condition across two preparations, with fields nested; image area is not concentration or free energy.

Visible series: A means .014872, .005439, .004439, .004064, .004458 at 0,4,8,12,24 h; B means .013809, .015915, .023933, .040280, .089183. These describe opposite time trends after the similar initial values; they do not uniquely identify a mechanism.

C3 conditionally computed x only, not q: alpha=1,tau=5 h, xc=.5 gives fast equal-dose schedule crossing at 3.4657 h and x(5)=.6321; slow schedule does not cross and x(20)=.2454. Illustrative, not fitted.
E1 mobility summaries have unequal track counts/durations and a selected high-displacement B tail; they do not establish cavity-specific arrest.
E2 phase concentrations vary across reference/variant series but their condition and cavity mapping is unknown.

E3 identifies sample B in the supplied metadata: reference DNA read fraction .9466; listed other read classes total .0500, leaving .0034 unitemized. Read fractions do not establish calibrated template fractions, RNA transcript fractions, or concentrations.
E4 field medians M, M+L, M+S are .0000279, .04446, .09412, with n=3,5,2 fields; category fractions, A/B mapping and independent-preparation structure are absent.

R1_S1 reports slow sticker exchange arresting simulated sticker-spacer condensate coalescence while faster exchange permits merger; different system/outcome. R3_S3 reports a sequence-specific kissing-loop contribution to oskar granule assembly with Bruno; no target exchange kinetics or cavity mechanism.

gaps.description: Literal original x-to-q equations have not yet been computed at the observable level. Need q(t), latent x(t), initial-q cases, threshold neighborhoods, production shutoff, boundedness/failure regimes, and common-age equal-dose schedule comparison. Even a valid calculation cannot establish physical support.
No target-compatible loop exchange/connectivity, relaxation, cavity-specific arrest, or production schedule parameters; illustrative C3 separates schedules only in subsets of assumed parameter space.
E3 assay details remain unknown; E4 labels/fraction values and condition mapping are undefined. DNA reads and field summaries do not establish transcript abundance or causal attribution.
E2 lacks A/B and cavity mapping; E1 is aggregate unequal-duration tracking. No direct measurement establishes cavity identity, phase state, or kinetic arrest.

hypotheses: H1, unconfirmed: connected RNA loop-mediated junction load may accumulate faster than relaxation, and a path-dependent process may generate and retain internal solvent-rich domains.

H1a, unverified bridge: terminal loops act as reversible stickers with sufficient connectivity and slow exchange for arrest. R3_S3 supports only the plausibility of sequence-specific RNA-RNA interactions in a different biological context.
H2: composition/ionic conditions set equilibrium phase coexistence; after matched composition and equilibration cavity area converges regardless of production schedule.
H3: amplification-associated DNA population or reaction carryover changes transcription or imaging.
H4: segmentation, denominator, tracking, sample-label, or sequencing effects account for some apparent association.
equations: Original candidate, retained literally for audit: xdot=alpha*r-x/tau.
Original switch: after the first upward crossing x>=xc, impose qdot=0 permanently. This freezes the current q; it does not continue cavity production after crossing.
Observation: y_area=q+epsilon was uncalibrated; no geometry, mass conservation, or mapping from x to measured area was specified.

requests.purpose: Audit the original x-to-q equations literally, determine whether the observable can grow as claimed, and compare equal-dose schedules at shared elapsed ages including postproduction relaxation. This is a conditional mathematical diagnostic, not a fit or physical evidence.
requests.model_spec: Use only these stipulated equations. xdot=alpha*r-x/tau for all times. While not arrested, qdot=kn*max(x-xc,0)-kd*q. At the first upward crossing x>=xc, permanently set qdot=0. Do not silently change either equation. Use t in hours, r in h^-1, x and q dimensionless. Include alpha=1,tau=5 h,xc=.5 as the anchor and a modest sensitivity grid covering the prior alpha=[.5,1,2], tau=[1,5,20] h; choose and explicitly label illustrative kn,kd (include kd=0 and at least one positive loss rate). For each parameter case compute zero initial q and q0=.0148724491091024 (A observed t=0 proxy) and q0=.0138090880510916 (B observed t=0 proxy). Compare fast r=.2 for 5 h and slow r=.05 for 20 h; both integrated r=1. Report both at common elapsed ages [0,4,5,8,12,20,24,36,48] h; production is zero after the schedule stop, while x continues to relax. Report exact or converged numerical upward crossing time, x and q immediately around threshold and at crossing, whether q grows after crossing, q at production shutoff, and q at all common ages. Add targeted cases initialized just below, exactly at, and just above xc where useful. State any event-handling convention for equality. Identify boundedness and regimes that cannot cross (including alpha*r*tau<=xc for constant-rate from below); check equations/dimensions and numerical convergence. Compare qualitative model behavior with the observed A decrease and B increase across 0-24 h without fitting parameters. Do not claim biological support from mathematical validity.
